inputs: Parsed ADC/legacy upload request, requesting UserConnection, slot-hook results, dynamic slot-limit settings.
preconditions: A resolved share profile and valid requested file are needed before slot selection.
defaults: Extra slot and last grant initialize to 0 via IGETSET.
effects: Selects existing permanent slot first; applies ActionHook slot grants (highest normalized grant); enforces MCN per-user/free-slot constraints; small-file MCN connections may use fileslot up to the source-coded threshold; standard slots depend on free capacity and upload-queue eligibility; minislot requires peer support plus existing minislot, operator status, or free extra slot. Slot type transition updates running/MCN/extra counts and lastGrant; excess MCN connections may be disconnected when low-speed allowance is unavailable.
errors: HookRejectException sends rejection message and disconnects; no slot sends maxed-out and may add failed request to user queue.
behavior.completion: Slot selection is synchronous within prepareFile under slotCS; it does not promise a slot until Created is fired.
behavior.cancellation: Connection rejection disconnects the request; slot allocation is reverted on connection removal.
resources: AutoLimitUtil dynamic slot limits, UploadQueueManager waitlist, UserConnection slot state, per-user MCN accounting.

ownership_evidence: UploadManager owns running user/MCN/small-file counters and tracks per-user MCN connections; source-count update is on slot transition (UploadManager.cpp:335-420).
threading_evidence: prepareFile serializes slot assignment with slotCS; updateSlotCounts can take cs through MCN bookkeeping.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Represent slot decisions as state outcomes and retain exact source-specific slot categories, counts, and rejection behavior.
acceptance_scenarios: Given all ordinary slots are occupied but a peer qualifies for an allowed minislot, when its request is prepared, then the parser grants a FILESLOT sourced as minislot and the extra-slot count increments.
Given a slot hook rejects a request, when prepareFile evaluates it, then the peer receives the hook rejection and is disconnected without creating an Upload.

inputs: UploadRequest type/path/segment; optional ADC user SID/list-recursive fields; hinted user/profile.
preconditions: Request path nonempty, start >=0, size not zero and >=-1; user identity must resolve to an online hub/profile.
defaults: Legacy requests use file type and resume position with unknown end; ADC optional ID/SID and RE/TL/ZL flags shape request parsing.
effects: Resolves profile by current hub hint or online-user SID; validates visibility and requested share object with UploadParser; assigns slot; opens/resumes stream; creates Upload and adds to active list; emits Created before slot counters update; removes wait-queue entry; ADC GET replies with SND carrying resolved range, optional ZL1/TL1; legacy GET replies with file length.
errors: Invalid request sends protocol error; unknown user sends ERROR_UNKNOWN_USER; parser maps no-access to ERROR_FILE_ACCESS_DENIED and missing file to ERROR_FILE_NOT_AVAILABLE; hook rejection sends its message; stream/share/queue/Core exceptions are converted to peer errors; zero/null upload failure sends generic error.
behavior.completion: Synchronous request admission through Upload creation; byte transfer starts immediately for ADC GET or after legacy Send callback.
behavior.cancellation: Failed admission disconnects on slot exhaustion/hook rejection; other failures leave connection handling to peer error/state path.
resources: Share profile visibility, ShareManager/parser, local InputStream/file handle, upload slots, UploadQueueManager, UserConnection.

ownership_evidence: UploadManager stores the created Upload in its owned uploads list; Upload takes ownership of InputStream (Upload.cpp and UploadManager.cpp:162-191).
threading_evidence: Request parsing and slot selection run synchronously on the UserConnection listener path; Created callback fires synchronously under slotCS.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Preserve protocol request validation, profile-specific share visibility, error distinctions, selected range and upload creation event; keep streams and C++ errors private.
acceptance_scenarios: Given a request with zero-length segment, when validation runs, then it is rejected before share lookup or slot assignment.
Given a valid file request from a known profile with a free standard slot, when it is parsed and prepared, then Created fires with its slot and ADC requests receive SND with the resolved segment.
Given an unknown hub SID, when preparing an ADC request, then the peer gets ERROR_UNKNOWN_USER and no Upload is created.

inputs: Exact file path and whether to wait for disconnect cleanup.
effects: Requests graceless disconnect for matching active and delayed uploads, including delayed uploads that retain file handles. With waiting enabled, polls both lists up to 20×250 ms for removal; logs error if still present after up to five seconds.
errors: No match is a no-op; timeout is reported only through error log, with no return/error value.
behavior.completion: Synchronous disconnect request; optional bounded wait for asynchronous cleanup, not guaranteed completion.
behavior.cancellation: This operation aborts matching transfers; actual removal occurs on connection/expiry callbacks.
resources: Active and delayed Upload lists, UserConnection disconnect, thread sleeps up to 5 seconds.

ownership_evidence: UploadManager owns active and delayed Upload lists; delayed entries retain their streams until cleanup.
threading_evidence: The method releases cs before polling; it sleeps 250 ms between up to 20 checks.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Expose abort as a request with bounded optional wait and explicit timeout outcome; do not promise that list removal always completes.
acceptance_scenarios: Given active and delayed uploads for the same path, when abortUpload is called, then both connections receive graceless disconnect requests.
Given a matching upload that remains after the wait window, when abortUpload returns, then it logs an abort timeout rather than claiming completion.

inputs: TransferToken for lookups and callback wrapper.
effects: Count and safe average use shared lock; unsafe average iterates active list without locking. Token lookup searches both active and delayed uploads. getAsyncWrapper captures token and callback, reacquires cs at invocation, resolves current pointer and invokes only if still present. Raw list and raw mutex are directly exposed; callers are synchronization/lifetime coupled.
behavior.completion: Synchronous reads; async wrapper executes later on caller-supplied dispatcher.
behavior.cancellation: No wrapper cancellation; callback is skipped if token no longer resolves.
resources: Manager-owned Upload pointer vectors and callback closure.

ownership_evidence: Active and delayed lists are exclusively owned by UploadManager; wrapper captures token, not pointer (UploadManager.cpp:505-531).
threading_evidence: Safe average/count lock cs; unsafe accessors do not; wrapper locks only for resolution then releases before callback, so callback cannot assume pointer remains valid unless execution is serialized to connection thread.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Expose copied snapshots and token-based guarded callbacks; do not expose raw Upload pointers, reference lists, or mutex.
acceptance_scenarios: Given a token for a delayed upload, when findUploadUnsafe searches, then it returns that upload; after deletion the async wrapper skips its callback.
Given concurrent upload mutation, when a bridge reads active uploads, then it copies a value snapshot under lock rather than retaining getUploads reference.

inputs: User identity; failed file path, start position and size; optional requested reconnect user.
effects: A full-slot failure inserts or updates a per-user wait entry and file item, updates connection token and resume position on repeated file request, then emits QueueAdd for a new file. Removing a queue removes all user file entries and notifications. A user is eligible when no queue/notifications exist or user has been notified. Each second available slots are assigned to queued online users and reconnect uses stored token; each minute expires notifications after 90 seconds and clears that user files. Queue snapshot copies users/files.
errors: Offline user connect returns nullopt; absent/unnotified user is not eligible. Queue update listener fires every second.
behavior.completion: Synchronous queue mutation; notification reconnect is issued after releasing queue lock.
behavior.cancellation: User queue removal clears the user wait state; offline-disconnect callback also clears queue.
persistence: Queue state is in-memory only; no persistence code in UploadQueueManager.
resources: ClientManager connection/reconnect; timer; queue and notified-user maps.

ownership_evidence: UploadQueueManager owns wait entries and UploadQueueItem shared pointers; clear emits item removal events then user removal under cs.
threading_evidence: Queue operations lock cs; Speaker callbacks are synchronous while queue lock is held; reconnect calls occur after lock release.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Expose queued-user/file snapshots and distinct item/user/update events; preserve in-memory queue and 90-second notification expiry.
acceptance_scenarios: Given an existing queued user retries the same file at a new resume position, when the request is denied for slots, then the existing item position/token are updated without adding a duplicate file.
Given one free slot and a queued online user, when the one-second notifier runs, then the user is marked notified, queue items are removed and the stored-token connection is requested.
Given a notified user does not claim the slot for 90 seconds, when the minute expiration runs, then that user’s queue files and notification are cleared.

Given a peer sends a bundle remove command for a tracked connection, when receiver parses it, then that connection is removed from the bundle association.

inputs: Upload construction binds a UserConnection, path/TTH and owned InputStream; queue item construction accepts hinted user, file, segment position and size; parser/request value constructors retain their supplied matching/request fields; upload bundle state accepts target/token/size/single-user/uploaded-byte count.
preconditions: UploadManager and UploadQueueManager constructors require initialized timer/client/settings/connection managers. Upload constructor requires a connection not already holding an upload and an owned input stream.
defaults: Upload::fileSize initializes -1. UploadManager/UploadQueueManager extra slot counters and grant timestamps initialize zero; UploadQueueManager extraPartial initializes zero. UploadBundle speed, totalSpeed, actual and uploadedSegments initialize zero; UploadQueueItem position is constructor supplied. UploadBundle clamps initial uploadedSegments to size when it exceeds size.
effects: Upload constructor initializes Transfer base, moves the InputStream into Upload, and associates itself with UserConnection; destructor clears the connection backpointer. UploadManager constructs its queue using a callback to getFreeSlots, registers as TimerManager listener and installs FREE_SLOTS_EXTENSIONS setting callback; destructor unregisters timer listener and waits until active uploads empty. UploadQueueManager stores the free-slot callback and registers with ClientManager/TimerManager; destructor unregisters and clears queued upload entries under lock. UploadBundle initializes aggregate upload values and removes its connection token on destruction. Bundle-info receiver registers/unregisters Timer, UploadManager and Protocol listeners. Sender registers DownloadManager/QueueManager listeners and conditionally advertises UBN1 based on USE_UPLOAD_BUNDLES; destructor removes these listeners. Inline UploadRequest/UploadParser constructors retain their request/parser inputs; WaitingUser conversion returns its contained UserPtr.
events: Upload lifecycle events are emitted by UploadManager operations inventoried in upload event records; constructor/destructor only establish and tear down listener/connection ownership.
errors: No constructor result status; UploadStream/manager dependency failures follow Core constructor behavior. UploadBundle initial uploaded byte count above size is clamped.
behavior.completion: Object construction and destruction are synchronous; UploadManager destruction can block until uploads drain.
behavior.cancellation: No object-level cancellation token; UploadManager abort operations remain in their operation records.
persistence: Upload queue and bundle persistence belong to their owning manager operations, not these value constructors.
resources: Upload uniquely owns its InputStream; UserConnection is a non-owning back-reference; UploadManager owns UploadQueueManager; bundle-info objects register as listeners and unregister during destruction.

ownership_evidence: Upload.cpp:30-40 moves stream into Upload and sets/clears UserConnection upload pointer. UploadManager.cpp:41-65 owns its queue and timer listener. UploadQueueManager.cpp:40-51 registers/removes ClientManager and TimerManager listeners. UploadBundle.cpp:28-36 removes its token on destruction.
threading_evidence: UploadManager destructor polls active uploads and checks collection under RLock; UploadQueueManager clears queue while holding WLock; remaining constructor-side listener registration is synchronous.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Bridge transfer objects through copied metadata and explicit lifecycle results; do not expose InputStream, Core listeners, or raw UserConnection pointers.
acceptance_scenarios: Given an Upload is constructed around a connection and input stream, when destroyed, then its connection backpointer is cleared and stream ownership ends with the object.
Given UploadBundle initial uploaded bytes exceed size, when constructed, then uploadedSegments is clamped to size.
Given UploadManager is destroyed with active uploads, when destruction starts, then the TimerManager listener is removed and destruction waits until the active upload list empties.
